I've spent 39 hours playing "Stick Fight: The Game," and I highly recommend it to anyone seeking a fun, chaotic multiplayer experience. This physics-based fighting game features simple controls and hilarious ragdoll physics, making it easy for anyone to pick up and enjoy. With over 100 interactive levels and a wide array of weapons, each match is unpredictable and entertaining. Whether you're playing locally with friends or online with players worldwide, "Stick Fight: The Game" offers endless laughter and excitement. Plus, it's available on multiple platforms, including Nintendo Switch, PC, and mobile devices, making it accessible for everyone.

Stick Fight: The Game is an absolute blast! It's a game that takes me back to those evenings with friends, gathered around the PC, laughing until our sides hurt. The best part? It's all about those stick figures we used to doodle in the margins of our notebooks.

The game's physics-based combat system is where the magic happens. Watching those stickmen flail around with ridiculous weapons, trying to take each other down, is pure entertainment. We'd spend hours sparring, trying out different levels and weapons, and just having a great time.

What's cool is that Stick Fight isn't just about the default levels. With the level editor and the massive collection of community-made levels, the fun never ends. There's always something new to try, some crazy level someone came up with, or a weapon combo that leaves us in stitches.

Sure, there's no single-player mode, but honestly, that's not what Stick Fight is about. It's about the chaotic fun of playing with friends, whether they're sitting next to you or joining in online. Plus, the procedural animations add that extra touch of hilarity to every match.

If you're looking for a game that's easy to pick up, endlessly entertaining, and perfect for those game nights with friends, Stick Fight: The Game is a must-have. It's simple, it's silly, and it's downright addictive. Highly recommended!

You know those party games, the ones that are really good to have running with a group of friends, but are really, really boring to play on your own? This is one of those.

The game itself is actually pretty fun despite being a bit barebones. Inspired by those fights we'd always draw in our school notebooks, up to four little wobbly stick figures duke it out in a physics-based arena. Weapons appear, some stranger than others (snake cannons?!), acting as a focus for the little wobbly sorts to frantically flop towards. There's the opportunity for upsets and turnarounds, making it a pretty fun party game as everyone tries to keep their streak. The arenas themselves cycle on a pattern, but there's enough for it to feel varied enough for a good, long session with some friends.

As an actual game pastime? I'unno, but it feels pretty fitting to have running in the corner of some social gathering, or for you and some friends to occupy yourselves with while you wait for the rest of the DnD group to show up or whatever.

The game is very fun and it is easy to get into matches and play with your friends or random people. However there is LOTS of issues with bugs and in my 4 hours of playing the game already this is what I've seen
-Sometimes players fall through the map when a new round starts
-The map doesn't load in and all players fall down to their death
-Players go through or get stuck inside walls/floor
-game freezes and screen goes black causing you to quit the game entirely and load back in
-when the host blocks certain weapons they show up anyway sometimes
-another player becomes invisable on your screen
-games lags and players start to fly around or walk somewhere under the map or not on the platform
This is pretty much it but most of the time these won't happen and you will have a pretty fun time.
I would reccomend this game and hopefully these issues are resolved in the future and if someone could please notify me when some of these issues are fixed that would be great.
